newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal nears upper limit, oil up on Sparks.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal nears upper limit, oil up on Sparks.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures were near the $10 per ton upper limit at midsession and soyoil futures were higher after Sparks Companies executive Willard Sparks forecast a rise in soybean futures, traders said.

Sparks told Reuters in an interview Tuesday that CBOT soybean prices are set to rise sharply, especially in the nearby months, because of tight U.S. soybean stocks. The U.S. Agriculture Department earlier this month put soybean ending stocks at a tight 125 million bushels.
Sparks' comments stirred ongoing concerns that tight soybean supplies will not last through the summer.

Floor sources noted last week's bidding war between soybean processors and exporters for what they perceive to be limited supplies. Farmer selling of soybeans have been slow all season and a recent span of dry weather has allowed farmers to turn their attention to seeding spring crops.
May soymeal drew further strength from the lack of deliveries against the May, although none had been expected. Conversely, heavy deliveries in soyoil capped gains.
At 1128 CDT, soymeal was up $7.80 to $2.30 per ton with July up $7.80 at $286.50 a ton. Soyoil was up 0.28 to 0.18 cent per lb with July up 0.21 at 25.47 cents.
